Spinner · four candidates and the one we ship

Every one below is live, at the four real sizes — 14, 16, 20 and 24px — on the page ground and inside a primary button, with the reduced-motion version beside it. Judge them at 14px. That is the size inside a small Button, and it is where most distinctive spinners quietly stop being legible.

The third column is the accessibility rule the system already committed to (D-024): under prefers-reduced-motion a spinner slows, it never freezes — a frozen spinner reads as a hung request.

Control — what ships today

A ring with one lit edge, turning. It is the spinner every framework ships, and it is what the brief asked to replace.

A · Comet

A conic tail chasing its own head. Pure CSS, no extra element, and the gradient does the work that a dashed stroke would — so it stays crisp at 14px where a thin arc starts to shimmer.

B · Arc

One stroke that lengthens and shortens as it turns, so the rhythm is a breath rather than a rate. Needs an SVG child; the round cap is what keeps it from reading as a fragment.

What does not change. Whichever wins keeps the same contract: role="status" with the label naming what is being waited for, or aria-hidden when adjacent text already says it; the four sizes; and the on-accent variant, because a spinner inside a filled button cannot use the raised-surface tone — it would be invisible.
